components.note: A person shape in the middle.
Two smaller marks pressing in from either side, like being sandwiched.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
辶 (to walk) — 违 involves stepping away from what is required, i.e. disobeying.
韦 (wéi) is an exact match for the sound of 违.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'
邦 (a nation/state) — a community bound together
巾 (a flag/cloth) — a banner people rally around to support one another
阝 (mound/place) suggests a hidden spot behind a hill.
急 (worried, urgent) suggests someone anxiously ducking out of sight, giving 隐 its meaning 'to hide, conceal.'
禾 (grain) — grain was one of the first things ancient people owned and kept for themselves.
厶 pictures something folded in on itself and hidden away, giving 私 its sense of 'private, personal, one's own.'
行 (to go/walk) — 街 names a road where people walk and travel.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
冂 (an enclosure or doorway) — 内 pictures the space one enters.
人 (person) — a person entering an enclosure gave 内 its meaning 'inside' or 'within.'
A drawing of a robe's collar and folded sides, seen from the front.
戌 (a halberd/weapon) — represents armed force.
女 (woman) — force used to intimidate gave 威 its meaning 'power, might, awe-inspiring.'
大 depicts a person, seen from the front with arms and legs spread.
弓 (a bow) shows the person carrying a weapon — together an early image of an armed outsider.
力 (strength/effort) — the exertion behind the achievement.
工 (work/labor) — results produced through skillful labor, giving 功 its meaning 'achievement, merit, skill.'
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'
⺮ (bamboo) — ancient texts were written on bound bamboo strips, and 第 originally referred to the sequential order of such strips, giving rise to its meaning 'ordinal number' (as in 第一, first).
日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
石 (stone) — 确 originally meant firm and solid like stone, extending to 'true, accurate, indeed.'
角 (jiǎo) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from què.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'
门 (gate, door) marks a boundary being crossed.
马 (horse) rushes through the gate — a horse charging in, giving 闯 its meaning 'to rush in, to dash.'
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.
方 here depicts a banner or flag flying from a pole, marking where troops are gathered.
疋 depicts a pair of marching feet — moving beneath the flag 方, the image gave 旋 its meaning 'to circle around, to return.'
车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'
片 (a thin slice/board) — 牌 names a flat board or sign, like a nameplate.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound close to pái.
牙 (tooth) — teeth piercing or boring through something, the origin of 'to pierce'
穴 (xué) gives a sound distantly related to 穿's reading chuān, having drifted apart considerably over time
走 (run/walk) — relates to 越's meaning 'to exceed, cross over,' running past a boundary.
戉 (yuè) gives the sound — 越 is also pronounced yuè, an exact match.
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.
回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
页 (head) — 顾 originally related to turning the head to look back at something
厄 (è) gives a sound distantly related to 顾's reading gù, having drifted apart over time
子 (child) forms the left side of the character.
小, standing in for a connecting thread in the traditional form 孫, links generations together, giving 孙 its meaning 'grandchild, descendant.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
扌 (hand) — 把 relates to grasping or holding something with the hand.
巴 (bā) gives the sound — 把 is pronounced bǎ, a close match differing only in tone.
扌 (hand) — 握 describes an action done with the hand: grasping tightly.
屋 (wū) gives a sound distantly related to wò, having drifted apart over time.
Woman — an old semantic root sometimes linked to feelings.
Gives the sound jiān, related to xián but drifted apart over time.
疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
灬 (fire) — 烈 relates to something as intense and fierce as fire
列 (liè) gives the sound — an exact match with 烈's reading liè
玉 (jade, shown without its dot) represents something valuable.
厶 beneath suggests something slipping away privately, giving 丢 its meaning 'to lose, to throw away.'
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.

meanings: camera (abbr. for 照相機|照相机[zhao4 xiang4 ji1])

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.
扌 (hand) — 授 means to give or hand something over.
受 (shòu) gives the sound — an exact match with 授.
木 (wood) — 权 originally meant a wooden lever or weight, later extended to 'power, authority, right.'
雚 was historically closer to guàn; the pronunciation has since shifted to quán, so the sound link is faint today.
豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'
乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'
龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.
贝 (money) — 贩 relates to trading for profit.
反 (fǎn) gives a sound close to fàn, differing only in tone.
扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.
耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.

meanings: (Tw) to repeatedly nod one's head while dozing

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows the material of the fishing hook.
勺 depicts a small curved shape, echoed in the curve of a fishing hook.
鱼 is a simplified picture of a fish — the top traces its head and fins, and the strokes below represent its body and tail.
八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.
隹 (a bird) — one of a flock.
木 (a tree) — birds flocking together on a tree, the image of gathering that gave 集 its meaning 'to gather, collect; a collection.'
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
立 (to stand) — 站 relates to standing, and by extension a stop or station where one stands to wait
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 站 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match
禾 (grain) — grain was one of the first things ancient people owned and kept for themselves.
厶 pictures something folded in on itself and hidden away, giving 私 its sense of 'private, personal, one's own.'
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
扌 (hand) shows 抚 relates to a gentle action done by hand.
无 (wú) gives a sound distantly related to fǔ, having drifted apart over time.
儿 (child) — 养 relates to raising and nurturing children or animals
羊 (yáng) gives a sound close to 养's reading yǎng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
禾 (grain) — an older sense of 秘 was linked to grain kept out of sight, before it narrowed to 'secret.'
必 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 秘.
⺺ — an abstract mark meant to depict strokes made by a writing brush, the origin of 书's meaning 'book, document, letter.'

meanings: (zoology) segment (of the body of a worm, centipede etc)

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, jade) — 环 originally referred to a round jade ring or bracelet
不 (bù) gives a sound distantly related to 环's reading huán, having drifted apart considerably over time
节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
亻 (person) — 伴 describes a person accompanying another.
半 (bàn) is an exact match for the sound of 伴.
Depicts two things splayed apart from each other — such as a bird's two wings, or two people standing back-to-back — later used for the meaning 'not, contrary to.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'
入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
止 (a foot, stepping forward) — 先 pictures someone moving ahead of another.
儿 (a person) — one person stepping ahead of another gave 先 its meaning 'before' or 'first.'

meanings: to be the one in charge

components.note: 讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.
⺮ (bamboo) — the material of ancient counting rods.
具 (held in two hands) — bamboo counting rods or an abacus held up for use, the tools of calculation that gave 算 its meaning 'to calculate, count.'
艹 (plant) — 蒂 names the stem that attaches a fruit or flower to its plant.
帝 (dì) gives the sound — an exact match with 蒂.
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
口 (mouth) — 啦 is a sentence-final particle, spoken from the mouth.
拉 (lā) is an exact match for the sound of 啦.
口 (mouth) — 啦 is a sentence-final particle, spoken from the mouth.
拉 (lā) is an exact match for the sound of 啦.
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.
饣 (food) — 饭 names cooked rice, a meal.
反 (fǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 饭.
丷 (horns) at the top shows the animal's horns.
田 (here shaped like a head with eyes) in the middle represents the animal's face.
口 (mouth) at the bottom completes the creature's face, giving 兽 its meaning 'beast, animal.'
土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
石 (stone) — 础 names the stone base of a pillar or building.
出 (chū) gives a sound distantly related to chǔ, having drifted apart over time.
